A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IRGS work. The complete main text and supplementary material, including Equations 1–18, Tables 1–3, and Figures 1–16, are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original IRGS benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative reconstruction and relighting experiments in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains the original IRGS benchmark results, ablations, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The differentiable 2D Gaussian tracer, two-stage optimization, losses, incident-light parameterization, and relighting procedure are unchanged in Sections 3 and 6. Added loss citations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Synthetic4Relight, TensoIR, and Stanford-ORB with the same tasks and scenes. The supplementary comparisons and composited-scene relighting demonstration are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain NeRFactor, InvRender, TensoIR, GS-IR, and R3DG as comparators. Figure 3 and the supplementary comparisons also retain their comparator sets. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, 40,000-plus-20,000 training iterations, 256-ray setting, 2^18 ray budget, and supplementary sampling procedures remain unchanged. Repositioning the implementation paragraph introduces no protocol change.

E4.justification: Table 3 and Figure 8 retain the same tests of indirect-light gradients, omission of indirect lighting during training or relighting, and sampled-ray counts. The supplementary illumination decompositions and qualitative analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical entries, including IRGS relighting PSNR of 34.90 in Table 1 and 29.907 in Table 2. The main and supplementary qualitative results are unchanged; the embedded figure images match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18, the dielectric-material assumption, ray–splat intersection derivation, and supplementary split-sum formulation are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about 2D Gaussian ray tracing, full rendering-equation evaluation, efficient optimization, and indirect radiance during relighting.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of indirect-light modeling and R3DG's novel-view-synthesis versus relighting tradeoff. The high-frame-rate limitation and suggested baking or precomputation remedies are unchanged, although the limitations paragraph moves.

D1.justification: Both disclose identical hyperparameters, learning rates, OptiX/CUDA implementation details, RTX 3090 hardware, training and rendering times, project URL, and supplementary relighting instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds NeRFReN and Reflective Gaussian Splatting as references 12 and 37. Section 3.3.1 adds explicit citations for existing distortion, smoothness, and mask losses. These modestly expand attribution and related-work coverage without revising the overall positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the Shanghai Innovation Institute affiliation, revises the corresponding-author footnote, and adds a funding acknowledgment. The substantive prose and section hierarchy are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Spacing and text-flow adjustments move Equation 17 from PDF page 6 to page 5 and Table 2 from the right to the left column on page 7. Printed page numbers disappear. All figures and tables retain their content and basic structure.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly documentation through explicit attribution of existing regularizers in Section 3.3.1 and two additional relevant references. The method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
